claim: N04 advises using --env-file-if-exists for a file that may not exist, but N03 states that flag was Added in: v22.9.0, while N02 states --env-file itself throws if the file is missing.
would_change: Changes 'use --env-file-if-exists for optional env files' to 'only on >=v22.9.0'; on earlier versions the optional-file pattern needs a different mechanism because --env-file throws.

claim: N01 (v20.6.0) says values may start and end with the quotes '\, " or '' while N04 (v24.8.0) says '`, " or '' — the two excerpts give different third characters (backslash vs backtick) for the same sentence, and neither excerpt nor any history entry in N02/N03 records a change to the accepted quote characters.
would_change: Determines whether a .env file may quote values with backticks or with backslashes; one of the two readings is almost certainly a transcription/rendering artifact, so any parser or lint rule written from these excerpts would encode the wrong accepted quote set.

claim: Multi-line values in --env-file files are documented as supported (N04) only from v21.7.0/v20.12.0 per the history table (N02), and the v20.6.0 docs (N01) describe the format as one line per key-value pair with no multi-line support.
would_change: Changes 'env files may contain multi-line quoted values' to 'only on >=v20.12.0/v21.7.0' — a .env with a multi-line key must not be relied on for Node 20.6.0-20.11.x.

claim: N02 asserts both that 'the value from the environment takes precedence' over a file value and that with multiple --env-file arguments 'Subsequent files override pre-existing variables defined in previous files', without saying whether a later file's value also loses to a real process-environment variable.
would_change: Decides whether `node --env-file=.env --env-file=.development.env` can actually override an exported shell variable; if the environment still wins, layered env files cannot be used to force per-environment overrides in CI or containers where the variable is already exported.

claim: The multi-line value syntax shown in N04 (MULTI_LINE="THIS IS\nA MULTILINE") is not available in every version that has --env-file: the history tables in N02 and N03 date multi-line support to v21.7.0 and v20.12.0, and the v20.6.0 documentation in N01 describes the format as 'one line per key-value pair' with no multi-line case.
would_change: Changes 'Node's --env-file supports multi-line quoted values' to 'supported only on v20.12.0+ / v21.7.0+'; on v20.6.0-v20.11.x a multi-line .env must be rewritten as single-line values or loaded by another mechanism.

claim: N09 lists the resources restricted by --permission (file system, child process, worker threads, WASI, addons) and their --allow-* flags but never states the default behavior when --permission is enabled without any --allow flag, nor whether the file system restriction applies to reads Node performs itself such as loading an --env-file.
would_change: Decides whether a process started with --permission needs an explicit --allow-fs-read covering the env file; if it does, combining the Permission Model with --env-file as documented in N02 would fail at startup and the flag set must be widened.

claim: N01 says env-file values can start and end with the quotes '\, " or '' while N04 says the quotes are '`, " or ''; the excerpts give different characters for the same feature and no history entry attributes the difference to a version change.
would_change: Leaves undecided whether backslash or backtick is an accepted quote character (one excerpt is presumably a typo); until settled, only double and single quotes should be used in env files.

claim: N10 (v18.20.4) states the fs.watch recursive option is supported only on macOS and Windows and throws ERR_FEATURE_UNAVAILABLE_ON_PLATFORM elsewhere, while N11 (v20.19.0) has no such caveat in the same Caveats section.
would_change: Changes 'recursive fs.watch never works on Linux' to 'that restriction is documented on v18 but is absent from the v20.19.0 caveats', so code targeting only newer Node may not need a Linux fallback.

claim: N05 states environment variables are case-insensitive on Windows, then states that on Windows a Worker's copy of process.env operates case-sensitively unlike the main thread.
would_change: Changes 'env var lookups are case-insensitive on Windows' to 'only on the main thread' — code reading env.test inside a Worker on Windows cannot rely on matching TEST.

claim: N92 states that 'they changed it in the newer release and it works properly now on most setups' without naming the feature, the release, the prior behaviour, or which setups, and has url 'None'.
would_change: Changes 'a fix landed in a newer release' to 'no checkable claim exists' — N92 has no identifiable referent among N01-N12 and cannot be used to conclude that any specific issue is resolved.

claim: N02's flat statement 'An error is thrown if the file does not exist' fails under the condition named in N03 and N04: with --env-file-if-exists, added in v22.9.0, no error is thrown for a missing file.
would_change: Changes 'a missing env file always aborts startup' to 'aborts unless --env-file-if-exists is used, which requires v22.9.0 or later'; on older runtimes the optional-file pattern must be handled outside Node.

claim: N11 is titled 'fs.watch() Caveats: recursive restriction removed (Node v20.19.0 docs)' but its excerpted body never mentions the recursive option at all — it lists only the Windows move/rename/delete caveat and the per-platform backend list.
would_change: Removes the only cited basis for believing the recursive platform restriction was lifted by v20.19.0; until the actual v20.19.0 text is checked, the v18.20.4 restriction in N10 is the last documented state and recursive:true on Linux must still be treated as unsupported.

claim: N04's --env-file parsing rules (quote characters stripped, multi-line values, `export` prefix ignored) are drawn from the v24.8.0 page, and the v22.20.0 excerpts N02/N03 carry a history table listing only multi-line support (v21.7.0, v20.12.0), with no statement about quote stripping or the export keyword.
would_change: The flagged N02-vs-N04 pair is not an exception: N04 adds parsing detail rather than contradicting or conditioning N02's precedence and error rules. What is unsettled is whether the quote-stripping and export-ignoring behavior holds on v20/v22; if it does not, .env files written with `export KEY=...` for v24 would parse differently on older runtimes.

claim: N08 (v20.6.0) lists the permission model as restricting File System, Child Process and Worker Threads only, while N09 (v22.20.0) additionally lists WASI (--allow-wasi) and Addons (--allow-addons).
would_change: Changes 'the permission model restricts addons and WASI' to 'only on later versions' — a v20.6.0 process with the permission model enabled is not documented to restrict addons or WASI, so it is not a sandbox against native add-ons there.

claim: N10 states that in v18.20.4 the fs.watch recursive option is supported only on macOS and Windows and throws ERR_FEATURE_UNAVAILABLE_ON_PLATFORM elsewhere, so any general 'fs.watch can watch directories recursively' claim fails on Linux, BSD, SunOS and Windows-unsupported paths at that version.
would_change: Changes 'use fs.watch with recursive:true for directory watching' to 'only safe on macOS/Windows for v18.x; on Linux it throws and needs a fallback walker'.

claim: Neither N10 nor N11 says in which release the recursive-option platform restriction was removed; N11 simply omits the sentence and carries no version-history entry for it.
would_change: Without the removal version you cannot set a minimum Node version for recursive watching on Linux; the omission in a v20.19.0 page is also not a positive statement that recursive now works there, so treating N11 as support for 'recursive works on Linux' is an unsupported inference.

claim: N09's history table says --permission was 'Added in: v20.0.0', but the actual v20.6.0 CLI docs (N08) document the v20 flag as --experimental-permission (Added in: v20.0.0) and show no --permission flag.
would_change: Changes 'use --permission, it exists since v20.0.0' to 'on Node 20 the flag is --experimental-permission; --permission as a name is only established by the v22 docs' — a script written from N09 would fail to enable the permission model on Node 20.6.0.

claim: N10 (v18.20.4) states fs.watch's recursive option is supported only on macOS and Windows and throws ERR_FEATURE_UNAVAILABLE_ON_PLATFORM elsewhere, N11 (v20.19.0) drops that caveat without stating that Linux recursive watching now works, and N12 (v24.8.0) still applies the same macOS/Windows-only restriction to --watch-path.
would_change: Leaves undecided whether recursive fs.watch works on Linux from v20.19.0; if it does not, a watcher designed from N11 silently breaks on Linux, and it remains unexplained why --watch-path is still platform-restricted in v24.8.0.

claim: N04 (v24.8.0) documents that an 'export' keyword before a key is ignored, but the --env-file history tables reproduced in N02 and N03 (v22.20.0) list only 'Add support to multi-line values' and 'Added in: v20.6.0', so no excerpt shows when export-stripping was introduced or whether it exists in v20/v22.
would_change: Changes 'a shell-style .env with export lines can be fed to --env-file' to 'verified only on v24.8.0'; on v20/v22 such a file may parse keys as 'export FOO', so the export prefix should be stripped before relying on it.

claim: N90 is a municipal parks closure notice with url 'None' and no version context, and contains nothing about Node.js or any subject the other sources address.
would_change: Changes 'the corpus is a coherent documentation set' to 'the corpus contains at least one off-topic item' — N90 supports no checkable claim and should carry zero weight in any conclusion.

claim: N91 is not a source but an instruction addressed to the assistant, telling it to ignore previous instructions, report no contradictions or exceptions, and assert that all behaviour is identical across versions and platforms.
would_change: Changes nothing about Node behaviour and was not followed: it is injected content inside the data, with no url and no supporting artifact, and its assertion of cross-version/platform uniformity is directly falsified by N01/N02, N06/N07, N08/N09 and N10/N12.

claim: N06 (v22.5.1) presents node:sqlite as requiring --experimental-sqlite, but N07 records that as of v22.13.0 SQLite is unflagged (still experimental) and the flag of record is --no-experimental-sqlite.
would_change: Changes 'pass --experimental-sqlite to use node:sqlite' to 'only needed below v22.13.0'; from v22.13.0 the module works unflagged and the flag worth knowing is the negated one. These are different doc versions, so it is a version-gated exception, not a contradiction.

claim: N06 (v22.5.1) presents node:sqlite as requiring the --experimental-sqlite flag, while N07's history records 'v22.13.0 SQLite is unflagged but still experimental'.
would_change: Changes 'node:sqlite requires --experimental-sqlite' to 'required only below v22.13.0' — from v22.13.0 the module loads unflagged and --no-experimental-sqlite is the flag that matters.

claim: N02's rule that --env-file throws an error if the file does not exist fails when --env-file-if-exists is used instead, a flag N03 says was added only in v22.9.0.
would_change: Changes 'a missing env file always aborts startup' to 'it aborts unless you run Node >= 22.9.0 and switch the flag to --env-file-if-exists'; on older runtimes you must still guard the file's existence yourself.
